## Giant Swarm conventions

devctl maintains this block and overwrites changes to it. Instructions for this repository go in the section below. Where they differ from this block, they take precedence.

- Never put customer names or other customer information in code, commit messages, issues or pull requests. Most Giant Swarm repositories are public, and private ones are kept ready to become public.
- Giant Swarm's style guides are in https://github.com/giantswarm/fmt, one directory per topic (go, helm, kubernetes, prometheus, …). Read the relevant guide before you write or review that kind of code.
- Use conventional commits for commit messages and pull request titles.
- If `.github/workflows/zz_generated.auto_release.yaml` exists, GitHub Releases are written from pull request titles: do not edit CHANGELOG.md. Otherwise, add your change to CHANGELOG.md as described in https://github.com/giantswarm/fmt/blob/main/releases/changelog.md.
- If `.pre-commit-config.yaml` exists, run `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` before committing; not every clone has the hooks installed.
- Do not add linters, formatters or other tooling unless asked; use what the repository already has.
- Put documentation in `docs/` rather than growing README.md, which gives an overview and links into `docs/`. When a change affects documented behaviour, update the documentation in the same pull request.
- If the skills of the `giantswarm/claude-code` plugin marketplace are not available to you and the user works at Giant Swarm, tell them once that they can install the `gs-base`, `gs-dev` and `gs-godev` plugins from it.
- Go: run `goimports -local github.com/giantswarm/<repository>` on the files you change. CI with architect-orb fails when imports are grouped differently.

# klausctl – agent context

## Repository layout

- `cmd/` -- Cobra command definitions (one file per command group)
- `pkg/` -- shared library packages
- `internal/` -- packages not intended for external import
- `docs/` -- narrative documentation

## Key packages

| Package | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `pkg/musterbridge` | Local lifecycle manager for the muster aggregator |
| `pkg/gatewaybridge` | Local lifecycle manager for `klaus-gateway` |
| `pkg/config` | Instance config loading, path resolution (`Paths` struct) |
| `pkg/mcpserverstore` | Read/write `mcpservers.yaml` |
| `pkg/runtime` | Docker/Podman detection and container operations |
| `internal/tools/muster` | MCP tool registration for the muster bridge |
| `internal/tools/gateway` | MCP tool registration for the gateway bridge |

## Bridge documentation

- [docs/musterbridge.md](docs/musterbridge.md) -- state files, ownership, MCP tools, troubleshooting
- [docs/gatewaybridge.md](docs/gatewaybridge.md) -- state files, ownership, MCP tools, troubleshooting

## Conventions

- Bridge packages expose `Start`, `Stop`, `GetStatus`, `EnsureRunning` functions.
- CLI surface and MCP tool inputs must stay in sync. The gateway bridge enforces
  this with a parity test in `cmd/gateway_parity_test.go`.
- State files follow strict ownership: klausctl owns PID/port files; users own
  config files. klausctl never writes to user-owned files.
- New tests go in `_test.go` files in the same package as the code under test.
